The fees and expenses payable pursuant to our technical and commercial ship management agreements with Technomar and Conchart, respectively, will be payable without regard to our business, results of operation, and financial condition and we have limited rights to terminate our management agreements.

material_events.basis: Stated in the cited 6-K press release (P5).
material_events.claim: GSL agreed a $1 billion seven-year syndicated loan facility at SOFR + 1.5% with an 8-bank syndicate led by Bank of America, to be drawn in tranches corresponding to delivery of each of the 15 Initial Newbuilds.
quotes: Global Ship Lease, Inc. (NYSE:GSL) (the "Company", Global Ship Lease" or "GSL"), a containership owner and lessor, announced today that it has agreed a $1 billion syndicated loan facility (the "New Facility") bearing an interest rate of SOFR + 1.5% and a duration of seven years.

The Company intends to draw on this facility in tranches corresponding to the delivery of each of the 15 newbuildings announced in June of this year (the "Initial Newbuilds"), the scheduled dates for which span from late 2028 through 2030.

material_events.basis: Stated in the cited Q2 2026 earnings release (P8) and H1 2026 6-K (P4).
material_events.claim: Moody's Investor Service upgraded GSL's Corporate Family Rating outlook from stable to positive, maintaining the Ba2 rating; Kroll Bond Rating Agency maintained BB+ with stable outlook and affirmed BBB/stable for the 5.69% Senior Secured Notes due 2027.
quotes: Moody's Investor Service maintained our Ba2 Corporate Family Rating, and upgraded to a positive outlook from a stable outlook. Kroll Bond Rating Agency maintained our corporate credit rating at BB+, with a stable outlook, while also affirming the BBB/stable investment grade rating and stable outlook for our 5.69% Senior Secured Notes due July 15, 2027 (the "2027 Secured Notes").

material_events.claim: GSL's Board declared a $0.10 per share increase in the quarterly supplemental dividend, raising the total annualized dividend to $2.50 per Class A common share ($0.625 per quarter), a 19.0% increase.
quotes: Our Board of Directors determined that sustained market demand for our fleet and our progress on securing forward fixtures at attractive levels supports a $0.10 per share increase in our quarterly supplemental dividend, amounting to a 19.0% increase in total annualized dividends per share, to $2.50 ($0.625 per quarter).

risks.claim: GSL's fleet has an average age of 18.4 years (TEU-weighted), and per-ownership-day operating costs rose 7.3% year-over-year, creating a structural cost headwind as vessels approach end-of-life.
quotes: Our operating fleet of 71 containerships as of June 30, 2026, had an average age weighted by TEU capacity of 18.4 years.
The average cost per ownership day for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $8,231, compared to $7,670 for the prior year period, up $560 per day, or 7.3%.
As our fleet ages, we may incur increased operating costs beyond normal inflation, which would adversely affect our results of operations.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (expiry count), P8 (contract cover percentages), and P2 (risk factor). Counter is stated in P8 and P4 (vessel table showing named charterers and future expiry dates).
risks.claim: Nine vessels (three expiring before H1 2026, six during H2 2026) face charter expiry, and rechartering at unprofitable or no rate would directly reduce revenue and cash flow.
quotes: The time charters for three of our 71 containerships either have expired or could expire before the end of the first half of 2026, and a further six vessels have charters that could expire during the second half of 2026.
100% contract cover for 2026 and 90% for 2027
We may be unable to recharter our vessels at profitable rates, if at all, upon their time charter expiry.

Our Executive Chairman is the Founder, Managing Director, and majority beneficial owner of Technomar and the sole beneficial owner of Conchart, our third-party technical and commercial ship managers.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (risk factors) and P3 (industry context). Counter is stated in P2 (orderbook composition), P3 (5.0% volume growth), and P6 (3.3-year average remaining charter term).
risks.claim: The container shipping industry is explicitly cyclical, with a 34.5% global orderbook-to-fleet ratio as of December 2025; a demand shock or oversupply correction could compress charter rates and vessel values simultaneously.
quotes: The container shipping industry is cyclical and volatile and our growth and long-term profitability depend mainly upon growth in demand for containerships, the condition of the charter market, and the availability of capital.

As at December 31, 2025, idle capacity of the global containership fleet was 0.8%, and the global containership orderbook to fleet ratio was 34.5%, which was weighted heavily towards containerships larger than 10,000 TEU.

A decrease in the export and/or import of containerized cargo or an increase in trade protectionism may harm our customers' business and, in turn, harm our business, results of operations, and financial condition.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (regulatory risk factor) and P3 (scrubber/ballast water cost note). Counter is inferred from P6/P8 (newbuild specifications) and P3 (drydocking cost data).
risks.claim: GSL faces escalating environmental and emissions compliance costs under EU ETS, FuelEU Maritime, ballast water rules, and potential scrubber retrofit requirements, which will increase operating expenses over time.
quotes: We are subject to evolving regulation and liability under environmental laws, including those related to emissions and decarbonization, which may adversely affect our revenues and profitability.

In future years there will be incremental costs for compliance with ballast water management regulations and with emission control regulations should we decide, in conjunction with our relevant charter, to retrofit scrubbers on our vessels.

risks.basis: Stated in P3 (debt breakdown, caps, cash, working capital) and P2 (debt risk factor). Counter is stated in P3 (caps, cash), P4/P8 (Moody's upgrade), and P5 (new facility margin).
risks.claim: GSL carries $694.7 million of debt with floating-rate exposure to SOFR, and while currently in compliance with covenants, a sustained rise in rates or a covenant breach would constrain refinancing and dividend capacity.
quotes: As at December 31, 2025, we had $694.7 million of debt outstanding, comprising $311.0 million of secured bank debt collateralized by vessels, $179.4 million of investment grade rated 2027 Secured Notes collateralized by vessels, and $204.3 million under sale and leaseback financing transactions, which have floating interest rates at SOFR plus a weighted average margin of approximately 2.34%.

We have substantial existing indebtedness and may incur more in the future. Our substantial indebtedness could adversely affect our ability to raise additional capital to fund our operations or pursue other business opportunities and may limit our ability to react to changes in the economy or our industry.
